# Source homotheties: exact parity filtration and a radial lattice obstruction

This note keeps the integer sum throughout. It gives exact cap and
first-moment formulas for dyadic contractions about an actual mixed
point, a valuation formula for mixtures of the contracted bodies, and
an obstruction to returning all parity cosets by inward radial maps.
It does not assert an OC inequality or a dyadic centering principle.

Relevant earlier results are:

* `candidate 438bf75c35923797`: every parity decimation can increase
  maximum depth, even with positive continuous dimension;
* `candidate d6a14443e8934b68`: exact
  integer ray-count densities need not be the angular density of a
  convex radial shadow;
* `candidate 9af97e78b545b0b8`: pairing two
  random points within each parity class gives an actual midpoint
  measure, with a sharp factor 2^n when all class densities overlap.

The construction below is instead contraction about ONE prescribed
actual point. Its arithmetic filtering and moment exponents are exact.

## 1. Exact contracted fibers, including every closed cap

Let C be a compact convex body in R^n times R^d, d>=1, with positive
mixed d-volume. Write K_z=C_z for its integer fibers, allowing empty or
zero-volume fibers. Fix an actual point y=(p,x) in C with p in Z^n.
For k>=0 put

    T_k(w)=y+2^(-k)(w-y),       C_k=T_k(C).

Convexity and y in C give C_(k+1) subset C_k subset C. For any integer
q, solving the base-coordinate equation gives the EXACT fiber identity

    (C_k)_q=x+2^(-k)(K_(p+2^k(q-p))-x).                (1)

Thus only original bases z congruent to p modulo 2^k appear. Conversely
every such nonempty original fiber appears at q=p+2^(-k)(z-p).

For a measurable body D write mu_D for its counting-in-base,
Lebesgue-in-fiber measure. Let mu be mu_C, and let mu^[k] be its
restriction to original bases z congruent to p modulo 2^k. Then as
measures on ambient space,

                  mu_(C_k)=2^(-kd) (T_k)_# mu^[k].       (2)

The factor is 2^(-kd), NOT 2^(-k(n+d)): only continuous fiber volume is
being changed by a Jacobian. The base sum is reindexed bijectively.

For an arbitrary affine cap threshold define

    H_s={ (z,w): a.(z-p)+u.(w-x)>=s }.

Here a and u may be zero individually, and closed boundary mass is
retained. Equation (2) gives

    mu_(C_k)(H_s)=2^(-kd) mu^[k](H_(2^k s)).            (3)

In particular EVERY through-y closed ambient halfspace obeys

    mu_(C_k)(H_0)=2^(-kd) mu^[k](H_0),
    mu_(C_k)(whole)=2^(-kd) mu^[k](whole).              (4)

These identities include oblique caps and purely integer caps. In the
latter case an entire fiber can lie on the cap boundary; it is included
on both sides of (3), without a null-boundary assumption.

Since C_k subset C, the left sides are genuine masses of nested actual
mixed bodies. Fiberwise, (1) is contained in K_q. Thus each positive
original congruent fiber forces an actual positive midpoint/iterated
midpoint fiber and the corresponding volume inequality. No arbitrary
assignment of a contracted fiber to a different base has been made.

If H_s contains y, then s<=0 and H_s subset H_(2^k s). Hence (3)
also implies mu_(C_k)(H_s)>=2^(-kd) mu^[k](H_s). For s=0 this is the
equality (4), rather than merely a cap-domination estimate.

## 2. First moments and the exact dyadic valuation invariant

The vector first moment about y has an ADDITIONAL contraction factor:

    integral (w-y) d mu_(C_k)(w)
       =2^(-k(d+1)) integral (w-y) d mu^[k](w).         (5)

Both base and continuous displacement components scale by 2^(-k).
When the filtered mass M_k is positive, its contracted centroid is

    g_(C_k)=y+2^(-k)(g^[k]-y).                         (6)

It equals y exactly if the original congruence-filtered centroid equals
y. Its convergence toward y by shrinking is not exact centering and
does not change the through-y cap fractions in (4).

For z!=p define

    nu_p(z)=max{ k>=0: z-p in 2^k Z^n },
    nu_p(p)=infinity.

Only finitely many integer fibers are nonempty. For large k the only
possible integer fiber of C_k is p. In particular the renormalized
mass 2^(kd) mu_(C_k)(whole)=M_k decreases to |K_p|; no original other
parity mass survives this repeated filtering.

There is an exact useful generating identity. Fix 0<tau<1 and define
the actual finite measure on the ORIGINAL mixed set

    R_tau=sum_(k>=0) tau^k mu_(C_k).                   (7)

It is finite, supported in S, and R_tau<=mu/(1-tau), since C_k subset C.
For a through-y cap H write

    m_z(H)=|K_z intersect H_z|,
    J_z=integral_(K_z) ((z,w)-y) dw,
    G_N(q)=sum_(k=0)^N q^k,
    G_infinity(q)=1/(1-q).

Tonelli and (4)--(5) give

    R_tau(H)=sum_z G_(nu_p(z))(tau 2^(-d)) m_z(H),      (8)

    integral (w-y) dR_tau(w)
       =sum_z G_(nu_p(z))(tau 2^(-d-1)) J_z.           (9)

Vector interchange in (9) is justified by boundedness of C and the
finite total measure; equivalently apply absolute convergence to each
coordinate. These are exact formulas on the original integer sum.

The cap/mass weight uses tau 2^(-d), while the centering weight uses
tau 2^(-d-1). They cannot be identified. The additional data are the
2-adic valuations of the actual displacement vectors z-p, rather than
only the number of occupied parity classes. Equations (8)--(9) are a
concrete arithmetic/radial invariant, not a conclusion that the right
side of (9) vanishes.

For a general nonnegative summable sequence of coefficients, the same
proof replaces G_N by the corresponding finite/truncated generating
sum. No convexity or logconcavity of the resulting mixed density is
implied by its construction as a sum of nested-body measures.

## 3. Pooling all parity cosets changes the lattice

Let r range over the 2^n residue classes modulo 2 and let mu_r be the
restriction of mu to class r. Under T_1, that class lands on the shifted
lattice

                    (p+r)/2 + Z^n.                    (10)

These are distinct cosets. Exactly the class r=p modulo 2 lands on the
original Z^n. Defining eta_r=2^(-d)(T_1)_#mu_r gives

    sum_r eta_r=mu_(T_1 C), measured on (1/2)Z^n,
    eta_r(H_0)=2^(-d) mu_r(H_0).                       (11)

The first equality uses the HALF lattice, not the original mixed
measure on Z^n. Although T_1 C subset C, its other coset measures are
not measures on the original mixed set.

If M_r>0 and g_r is the original class centroid, then

    eta_r(whole)=2^(-d)M_r,
    centroid(eta_r)=(y+g_r)/2.                        (12)

For nonnegative class weights c_r, not all zero on occupied classes,
the pooled measure has centroid y exactly when

                   sum_r c_r M_r (g_r-y)=0.            (13)

Allowing zero weights, such a choice exists iff y lies in the convex
hull of the occupied class centroids. If every class is retained with
a positive weight, the corresponding criterion is relative-interior
membership in that convex hull. With all c_r=1, centering occurs iff
the TRUE original mixed centroid equals y. None of these statements
returns the other cosets to the original lattice.

For clarity, translating those cosets back does not preserve (11).
Choose representatives r=p+s with s in {0,1}^n and shift its contracted
base by -s/2. The resulting map is

    (z,w) -> ((p+z-s)/2, (x+w)/2).

Its through-y margin is

    [a.(z-p)+u.(w-x)-a.s]/2.                           (14)

Thus the old cap threshold becomes a.s, which depends on the oblique
base normal and the coset. Moreover the translated fiber need not lie
in C. For example take n=1, K_0=epsilon B_d, K_1=B_d,
0<epsilon<1/2, C their binary fiber hull, and y=(0,0).
The class-1 contracted fiber is (1/2)B_d at base 1/2. Shifting it to
base 0 is not contained in K_0. The original dyadic image is contained
in C, but this integer relabeling is not an actual compatible action.

## 4. Primitive fibers cannot move inward along their ambient rays

This is a stronger exact obstruction to a radial all-coset repair.
Let z!=p and let g be the greatest common divisor of the integer
coordinates of z-p, taken positive. For any w=(z,v) in that fiber,

    y+t(w-y) has integer base  iff  t in (1/g) Z.        (15)

The forward implication follows by an integer Bezout combination of
the coordinates of z-p: if t(z-p) is integer, then tg is integer.
The reverse is immediate because (z-p)/g is an integer vector.

Consequently, when z-p is primitive (g=1), its open segment to y has
NO points on the original integer-base lattice. The only points of
that closed ray segment in S are w itself and y. This conclusion is
independent of fiber shape or its continuous dimension.

In particular consider any measurable transport kernel from a
positive-volume primitive fiber, supported on the inward segments
[y,w]. If its output measure is absolutely continuous with respect
to original mixed d-volume, it cannot put positive mass at the point
y, since d>=1. Therefore the kernel must retain w itself almost
everywhere: this fiber is IMMOBILE under such an inward radial
transport. Randomization does not evade the conclusion. A finite
density domination by mu is a sufficient absolute-continuity premise.

Preserving incidence with EVERY through-y closed halfspace also
explains why radiality is the natural requirement here. For two
nonzero displacement vectors v,w, the equivalence

    [ell.v>=0 iff ell.w>=0] for every linear functional ell

holds iff w is a positive scalar multiple of v. To prove this, the
functionals vanishing on v must also vanish on w (apply both signs),
so w lies on its line, and a functional positive on v fixes the
positive orientation. The origin has different incidence and is not
an exception to this equivalence.

Thus a deterministic relocation preserving all through-source cap
incidences and strictly moving inward is impossible on primitive
fibers. The kernel statement assumes ray support directly; aggregate
equality of cap measures alone is not being equated with pointwise
incidence preservation. This distinction prevents an unsupported
claim about arbitrary nonradial measure couplings.

## 5. Even exact pooled centering does not supply ordinary Gamma_d

There is an actual, globally deepest calibration with no centering
defect. Let d=n>=2 and

    v_0=(-1,...,-1), v_i=e_i for 1<=i<=d,
    B=conv(v_0,...,v_d),
    P=B intersect Z^d={0,v_0,...,v_d}.

Let K be a d-simplex of volume V and centroid g, put C=B times K,
and take y=(0,g). Its TRUE mixed centroid is y, since the outer bases
sum to zero and every fiber centroid is g. All d+2 listed bases have
distinct parity, and each nonzero displacement from 0 is primitive.

The already independently audited source
`candidate d7fcf9727e1fd83d`
proves y is the unique global deepest point, with normalized depth

             beta=(1+Gamma_d)/(d+2),
             Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d.                     (16)

The relevant cap calculation is elementary and can be retained
without invoking that depth theorem. Write lambda_j for the continuous
simplex barycentrics, and define base functionals

    ell_0(z)=-sum_i z_i,
    ell_i(z)=(d+1)z_i-sum_l z_l.

They sum to zero, have ell_j(v_j)=d and ell_j(v_k)=-1 for k!=j.
Each through-y cap

    H_j={lambda_j(w)-1/(d+1)+ell_j(z)>=0}

captures Gamma_d V on the own fiber, one full outer fiber V, and no
other outer fiber. Its mass is (1+Gamma_d)V out of (d+2)V.

The all-coset measure in (11) is exactly centered at y, and every one
of these cap fractions is unchanged. Nevertheless beta<Gamma_d for
d>=2. Indeed Gamma_d>1/(d+1), by
(d/(d+1))^(d-1)>=2/(d+1) and 2d/(d+1)^2>1/(d+1).
For d=2 the fractions are 13/36<4/9. The pooled measure is a discrete
base sum on the half lattice, not a uniform convex-body measure to
which an ordinary Gamma_d theorem applies.

There is an ORIGINAL-lattice version using (7), so the defect cannot
be attributed only to half-lattice support. For every k>=1 the only
integer base of C_k is 0, and that fiber is
g+2^(-k)(K-g). It has centroid g and the displayed through-g cap
fraction Gamma_d. Hence EVERY nonnegative dyadic mixture

    R=sum_(k>=0) a_k mu_(C_k),
    a_0>0, A=sum_(k>=0) a_k 2^(-kd)<infinity,

has centroid y, total mass V[A+(d+1)a_0], and displayed cap mass
V[Gamma_d A+a_0]. Its fraction is strictly below Gamma_d because

    Gamma_d[A+(d+1)a_0]-[Gamma_d A+a_0]
       =[(d+1)Gamma_d-1]a_0>0.                        (17)

The measures are supported in the original mixed set. Summable a_k
even give the elementary bounded density R<=sum a_k mu. Dropping
a_0 entirely leaves only the central fiber; it also discards ALL the
original outer-fiber mass, so its ordinary guarantee is not a
full-family payment.

This is not an OC counterexample: beta is well above the mixed target,
and the original example has heavy-fiber equality. It refutes the
specific inference that pooling parity/radial contractions and
centering their actual measure makes the ordinary Gamma_d bound
available without additional geometric information. Equations
(8)--(9), (13), and the primitive-ray restriction (15) identify the
arithmetic and moment data that such an additional argument would
have to retain.
